problems.problem: The regenerated sweep now carries the diagonal corner-to-corner (enters left edge y≈790, exits bottom-right corner), fixing the dead lower-right quadrant of the previous version, but the fold renders as a saturated teal wedge: a near-solid #2b7fa0 band roughly 25-40px wide with an abrupt upper edge, widening toward the corner, instead of the 'gently diffused' shadow of matte paper in the declared concept. It reads as a printed graphic stripe against the pale #bfd6de field and clashes with the soft frontal light on the bottle. No studio equipment artifacts are present; the fault is折 hardness and saturation.

Contact detail crop [132,1141,668,1391] confirms the bottle is correctly seated: a soft grey smudge hugs the base at canvas y≈1276-1290, offset_y 0 is correct and must not be moved, and the base at y=1281 (89% of canvas height) respects the margin bounds. However the smudge spans only about x≈290-500 against the 376px base footprint (bbox 212-588) and stays faint at poster scale, so the dark glass still reads slightly pasted onto the sweep. The cue needs width and presence, not repositioning.

The right-aligned stack (logo y79, title y168 at size 46, subtitle y300, rule y324) ends 957px above the bottle base, leaving the mid-right field between the rule and the fold empty; type and product read as two islands joined only by the diagonal. text_product_overlap is false for all three blocks, so this is scale/anchoring, not collision: against references that deploy type as a confident graphic mass (Prada's oversized serif block), Georgia at 46px on a 1080px canvas remains modest.
